ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the left half-cell has a Cu metal electrode inserted into a solution labeled CuNO3, corresponding to the Cu/Cu+ half-cell; the right half-cell has a Zn metal electrode inserted into a solution labeled Zn(NO3)2, corresponding to the Zn/Zn2+ half-cell. The two sides are connected by a salt bridge labeled NaBr, and above there is an external circuit connecting the two electrodes. The overall reaction printed below the figure is 2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq), and E° = +1.28 V is given. Reasoning: From the overall reaction in the figure, the reaction quotient can be written as Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu+]^2, because the solids Zn(s) and Cu(s) do not enter Q. According to the Nernst equation E = E° - (RT/nF)lnQ, this reaction transfers n = 2 electrons. If [Zn2+] increases as the reaction proceeds, while other concentration conditions remain unchanged, then Q increases and lnQ increases, so the term subtracted from E° becomes larger, therefore the overall cell voltage E becomes smaller.
